safety.note: Giredestrant's discovery paper claims excellent in vivo safety; the species are rat and dog toxicology, the same package later filed for vepdegestrant.
safety.quote: 35 exhibits low drug-drug interaction liability and demonstrates excellent in vitro and in vivo safety profiles.
safety.judgement: Separate safety track: GLP toxicology species are a different system from the efficacy xenografts and make their own prediction.

safety.magnitude_basis: stated clean animal profile vs AE rates balanced against standard endocrine therapy
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year is the NCT04576455 results posting (2023-03-10). The stated prediction is qualitative, so the match is direction only; bradycardia, a known class signal, is not reported in the abstract either way.
safety.model: Rat and dog repeat-dose toxicology (oral ER degraders)
safety.note: acelERA: giredestrant's grade 3-4, serious and discontinuation AEs were balanced against physician's-choice endocrine therapy.
safety.short: Giredestrant safety matched prediction in acelERA
safety.quote: Giredestrant was well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to PCET and consistent with known endocrine therapy risks.
safety.judgement: The model's stated prediction (excellent in vivo safety) held in a randomised comparison. Thin but admissible: a stated prediction, a patient comparison, both quoted.

safety.magnitude_basis: dog repeat-dose ECG QT/QTc prolongation vs patient mean ΔQTcF 10.9 ms (QTc prolongation an adverse event of special interest, 8.4% any grade)
safety.confidence_note: FDA multidisciplinary review, nonclinical summary (FDA-authored). hERG was negative to 30 µM and a single-dose dog cardiovascular study was clean; the repeat-dose dog ECG finding is the prediction that held. The leukocyte and haemoglobin decreases in patients were not apparent in rats or dogs, which the reviewer treats as corresponding to bone-marrow and liver findings rather than as a miss.
safety.model: Rat and dog repeat-dose toxicology (oral ER degraders)
safety.note: Dogs showed QT/QTc/PR prolongation and liver-weight gain on repeat dosing; patients had QTc prolongation (mean ΔQTcF 10.9 ms) and AST rises, but the haematology falls were not seen in animals.
safety.short: Dog QT prolongation foretold patient QTc
safety.quote: While adverse changes in hematology and clinical chemistry were not apparent in animal studies, corresponding findings were observed, including increases in liver weights and prolonged electrocardiogram QT-, QTc- and PR-intervals in dogs.
safety.reason: Dog ECG predicted QTc; blood counts missed
safety.judgement: Stated comparison by the regulator, scored same with source_calls_it partial: the clinically important harm (QTc prolongation, an AESI with label language) was predicted in dogs; the mostly low-grade haematology changes were not, and I did not open a contra for them because the reviewer classes them as corresponding to the animal bone-marrow findings. Counted once, here.

safety.confidence_note: FDA-authored nonclinical assessment summarising the sponsor's safety-pharmacology reports, which were not read. The studies were run pre-IND (unpublished), so 2026 is a proxy first-use year; the class's GDC-0810-era hERG data were not found in print.
safety.note: Vepdegestrant's ICH S7 battery: hERG negative to 30 µM (>1000x free Cmax), single-dose dog telemetry clean at 400 mg/kg; no CV liability predicted.
safety.short: hERG and dog telemetry predict no CV effect
safety.quote: Vepdegestrant had no effect on hERG tail current at concentrations up to 30 µM (the limit of solubility) when compared with vehicle-treated cells.
safety.judgement: Opened as its own track: the standalone safety-pharmacology battery (in-vitro hERG plus single-dose telemetry) is a different system from the repeat-dose rat/dog toxicology track and made the opposite prediction (no cardiovascular effect) from the repeat-dose dog ECG (QT/QTc/PR prolongation).
safety.model: Safety-pharmacology core battery: hERG patch-clamp and single-dose conscious-dog cardiovascular telemetry (vepdegestrant)

safety.magnitude_basis: hERG no effect to 30 µM (>1000x free Cmax) and single-dose dog telemetry clean at 400 mg/kg (10x free Cmax) versus patient mean ΔQTcF 10.9 ms (90% CI 8.2-13.6), label section 5.1 QTc warning
safety.confidence_note: Both sides are in the same FDA review (nonclinical section lines ~1882-1888; clinical section line ~1064) but the review never reconciles them, so this is a pairing I made, hatched. The 10-fold dog margin is on free Cmax; the dog study is single-dose, so a repeat-dose effect was outside what it could show, yet the hERG result at >1000x free Cmax is a direct miss. Registry date is the VERITAC-2 (NCT05654623) results posting.
safety.note: Patients on 200 mg showed mean ΔQTcF 10.9 ms, 11% TdP/QT SMQ events vs 1% on fulvestrant, and a label QTc warning; none predicted.
safety.short: Clean hERG and dog telemetry, patients prolonged QTc
safety.quote: Notably, vepdegestrant is associated with QTc prolongation (mean ΔQTcF: 10.9 msec [90% CI: 8.2 to 13.6 msec]).
safety.reason: hERG, dog telemetry clean; patients prolonged QTc
safety.judgement: Contra, not pooled into the repeat-dose track's same/partial: the run's track-identity rule keeps a different model with a different prediction apart, and the count-once rule is satisfied because the repeat-dose dog track already carries the harm as predicted; this track records the component that predicted wrongly. Magnitude direction_only, as other hERG/telemetry misses in the atlas; the review does not call it, so source_calls_it is null.
safety.model: Safety-pharmacology core battery: hERG patch-clamp and single-dose conscious-dog cardiovascular telemetry (vepdegestrant)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Europe PMC; the paper is open access but the figures were not opened). First use of this system for the class is this paper.
safety.note: Zebrafish embryos dosed with oral SERDs to explain the bradycardia seen with giredestrant and camizestrant in trials; built after the clinical signal.
safety.short: Zebrafish model built for SERD bradycardia
safety.quote: To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanism, we used chemical biology and genetic approaches in a zebrafish model of SERD-induced bradycardia.
safety.judgement: Opening entry for a retrodiction model: the clinical bradycardia (giredestrant dose-related heart-rate fall, phase Ia/b) was known before the model was built, so any match can only score retro.
safety.model: Zebrafish embryo heart-rate model of SERD-induced bradycardia (wild-type and esr1/esr2/gper mutants)

safety.magnitude_basis: presence or absence of bradycardia per SERD in zebrafish embryos versus clinical reports: giredestrant and camizestrant positive, amcenestrant and fulvestrant negative in both
safety.confidence_note: Patient side is as the paper states it (giredestrant bradycardia from its phase Ia/b and C-QTc reports; amcenestrant none in AMEERA trials); the trial papers were not re-read for heart-rate tables. Camizestrant is not a member and does not score.
safety.note: Giredestrant slowed zebrafish hearts and amcenestrant did not, matching which members cause bradycardia in patients; esr1 mutants were protected, so on-target.
safety.quote: Giredestrant and camizestrant induced significant bradycardia in wild-type zebrafish embryos, whereas fulvestrant and amcenestrant (SERDs that do not induce bradycardia in patients) did not alter heart rate.
safety.reason: Reproduced which SERDs slow the heart
safety.judgement: Retro, not same: the model was run after the clinic knew the answer (decision 10). Scored on the two members it dosed (giredestrant positive, amcenestrant negative), both reproduced; the esr1-mutant rescue adds mechanism (on-target ER signalling) that the repeat-dose rat/dog track never offered. Class-level: it separates molecules, not patients.
safety.model: Zebrafish embryo heart-rate model of SERD-induced bradycardia (wild-type and esr1/esr2/gper mutants)
